title: Anthology and prose retrieval quiz
subject: English Literature
source: Seeded from english-literature/y11 lesson 47 (Anthology and prose retrieval quiz (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 46 to 51 of Final preparation. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: A prose paragraph retells the plot well but has no argument. Best repair?
options: open with a claim about Steinbeck's purpose and use the plot as evidence
questions.a: A) open with a claim about Steinbeck's purpose and use the plot as evidence. The prose essay rewards argument and context, not retelling.

questions.q: Which revision method builds memory best?
options: closing the book and writing what you remember, then checking
questions.a: B) closing the book and writing what you remember, then checking. Retrieval practice is stronger than rereading.

questions.q: What is the turning point of 'Hands'?
options: 'She calls me by my mother's name.'
questions.a: C) 'She calls me by my mother's name.'. The second stanza opens with the loss of memory made painfully clear.

questions.q: How should you use the clean text in Component 2?
options: go straight to moments you already know and quote briefly
reread the whole play during the exam
questions.a: A) go straight to moments you already know and quote briefly. Knowledge of where things are saves time.

questions.q: You cannot remember an exact quotation in the prose essay. Best move?
options: refer precisely to the moment and analyse it
questions.a: B) refer precisely to the moment and analyse it. Precise reference to a moment still earns credit; never invent a quotation.

questions.q: Which thesis is strongest for 'How does Priestley present Sheila?'
options: Sheila is a character in the play.
Sheila is the daughter of Mr Birling.
Priestley uses Sheila to show that the young can learn responsibility, unlike their parents.
questions.a: C) Priestley uses Sheila to show that the young can learn responsibility, unlike their parents.. An arguable claim about the writer's purpose.
